subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 13 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept all 13 executable action revisions together after final-head gates, including the Codex v1.11 permission and sandbox implementation?
rationale: The patch is mechanically clean, but accepting new code that receives credentials, repository permissions, release access, or agent execution authority requires owner intent and direct dependency-contract verification.

options.title: Verify and land together
options.body: Approve the grouped immutable revisions after direct Codex runtime inspection and all relevant security, workflow, release, and dependency checks pass on one stable head.

options.title: Split sensitive actions
options.body: Move Codex, token-creation, registry-login, and release-action bumps into separately reviewed PRs while allowing lower-risk setup and maintenance actions to proceed independently.

options.title: Pause the group
options.body: Leave the update unmerged until Dependabot repository access and stable-head rebasing are restored.

recommendation.title: Verify and land together
recommendation.body: Approve the grouped immutable revisions after direct Codex runtime inspection and all relevant security, workflow, release, and dependency checks pass on one stable head.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows broad recent ownership of central CI and release workflow behavior, making this person the strongest routing candidate for the grouped security-boundary decision.
